messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: HIGH severity — p99 tail latency spike detected for single-tenant deployment 'catalystmed-prod' (dedicated-pool-7). Metric: streaming p99 5.8s (SLO 1.5s). Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream (model: redwood/gptx-3.2b-q4). Pager: oncall-alice.

alice: ack. joining. noticed alerts for increased stream stalls + connection resets. marking incident and opening thread here. @raj @maria @tom can you triage? :eyes:

raj: on it. initial check: high queue length on pool-7 workers, heavy long-prefix requests from catalystmed that keep KV cache entries pinned. sample log tail: ```
2026-03-15T02:17:42Z worker-7 WARN kv_cache_evictions=0 cache_hits=0 active_prefixes=1123
2026-03-15T02:18:01Z worker-7 ERR stream_abort reason=write_timeout conn_id=0x3f2a
```

maria: rounding up infra: autoscaler on dedicated pools shows saturation at 98% for the last 6m; no recent deploy. network egress steady. we're on GCP us-central1. Could increase pool or add burst nodes, but that's a slower mitigation.

tom: runtime note — this model variant is q4 quantized and CPU fallback behavior has slightly higher memory pressure. If prefix churn is high, KV cache thrash will blow p99. Quick mitigations: 1) enable prefix_kv_eviction_policy=LRU with lower capacity, 2) route catalystmed to compatible model variant with smaller KV footprint (redwood/gptx-3.2b-q4-small-kv) as fallback, 3) temporarily increase pool size (maria).

alice: immediate actions: (1) set fallback route to q4-small-kv for catalystmed, (2) evict oldest KV entries on pool-7, (3) inform customer via catalyst-support-bot. I'm executing (1) now.

alice: /infra route update --customer catalystmed --from redwood/gptx-3.2b-q4 --to redwood/gptx-3.2b-q4-small-kv --sticky 30m

incident-bot: ACTION_LOG: route update queued -> applied in 14s.

catalyst-support-bot: Automated message queued to CatalystMed (SLA contact): "We're investigating degraded streaming performance for your production tenant. Mitigation steps are being applied — short-term routing change and cache eviction. Expect follow-up in 30m."

raj: after route flip, observed p99 dropped to ~1.8s within 45s for in-flight streams. However some long-lived sessions still show intermittent stalls due to backlog. Stack trace snippet from runtime: ```
2026-03-15T02:19:05Z worker-9 INFO accept request id=0x8ab4 prefix_len=3200 tokens
2026-03-15T02:19:09Z worker-9 WARN kv_cache_lock_wait_ms=4200
```

maria: spun up 3 burst nodes in pool-7 (n1-highmem-8) — added capacity pushed saturation to 62%. New nodes registered and started accepting streams in ~70s.

tom: also toggled prefix_kv_eviction_policy=LRU and lowered kv_capacity to 256MB on pool-7. Command: ```
# runtime config
set pool-7.kv.capacity=256MB
set pool-7.kv.eviction=LRU
```

alice: status update: p95 back to 0.9s, p99 stabilized around 1.4s across new traffic (last 5m). Customers on streaming still saw ~10% of requests with stalls during the window; we've kept a short-term route fallback for 30m. Will monitor.

sophia: product/CS note — CatalystMed reported some user-visible degraded responses earlier. I've drafted a proactive customer message: "We applied a temporary routing and capacity change that should restore streaming performance. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a root-cause summary and timeline." Want approval to send after next check.

alice: approved. send after 15m if metrics stable.

raj: hypothesis for postmortem: single-tenant long-prefix pattern (very long system messages + few-shot examples per request) created KV population blowup; combined with quantized model memory characteristics caused eviction starvation and lock contention, exacerbated by high concurrency from CatalystMed's batch jobs. Repro steps noted.

tom: mitigation plan to include: 1) add adaptive kv_capacity per-tenant (limit worst offenders), 2) better default eviction heuristics (age+size), 3) route suggestion in console to auto-fallback to smaller-kv variants when prefix_len > 1024, 4) add early backpressure (503) for sessions exceeding prefix+concurrent token budget.

maria: infra follow-ups: 1) allow faster burst capacity provisioning for dedicated pools (reduce instance spin-up from ~45s to ~20s), 2) alerting to include kv_lock_wait_ms > 2000ms as a trigger.

alice: creating incident ticket and assigning postmortem. ticket: INC-2026-1874. I'm handing off monitoring to night-oncall (tom) at 02:50Z. if anything regresses, escalate to eng-runtime and ML.

tom: taking handoff. current snapshot: p95=0.88s p99=1.35s active_connections=842 pool-7.sat=62% fallback_active=true. Leaving route fallback active until 03:30Z unless metrics good.

sophia: added a customer follow-up note to the ticket and linked the outgoing message draft.

alice: final: thanks team. will capture timeline + logs for postmortem. ACTIONS_OWNER: raj (repro + eval harness), tom (runtime fix proposal), maria (autoscaler speedup), sophia (customer comms). closing pager. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: RESOLVE: page resolved by alice at 1765123956. Incident severity -> SEV2. Postmortem required.
